competences: The learner explain unless as if not.
The learner punctuate unless-clauses at the beginning and in the middle.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and uses correctly: unless, condition, if not, comma.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explain unless as if not.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to punctuate unless-clauses at the beginning and in the middle.
priorKnowledge: Learners have identified conditions and punctuated sentences beginning with if.
materials: Unless sentence strips showing two clause positions
references: P4 English End Of Term III 2023

steps.content: Learners have identified conditions and punctuated sentences beginning with if. Key words: unless, condition, if not, comma
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays unless sentence strips showing two clause positions and links the chart to the prior knowledge: Learners have identified conditions and punctuated sentences beginning with if. The teacher pronounces the lesson vocabulary, checks learners’ reading, and introduces using unless.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall familiar words, read the displayed key words aloud, and explain what they already know about the topic.

steps.content: Using unless: Unless means “if not”. A comma follows an unless-clause placed at the beginning. A comma is not required before unless in the middle.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: Unless means “if not”. A comma follows an unless-clause placed at the beginning. A comma is not required before unless in the middle. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Punctuate: unless he listens to his teacher he won’t learn" Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

steps.content: Example 1: If you don’t go to bed early, you will feel tired. Unless you go to bed early, you will get tired.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: If you don’t go to bed early, you will feel tired. Unless you go to bed early, you will get tired. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Punctuate: unless you go to bed early you will get tired" Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: Unless you go to bed early, you will get tired

steps.content: Example 2: Unless he listens to his teacher, he won’t learn. The condition comes first. A comma separates the condition from the main clause.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: Unless he listens to his teacher, he won’t learn. The condition comes first. A comma separates the condition from the main clause. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Read and write correctly: do not open this booklet unless you are told to do so" Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: Unless he listens to his teacher, he won’t learn

steps.content: Example 3: Do not open this booklet unless you are told to do so. The unless-clause comes after the main clause. No comma is needed before unless here.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: Do not open this booklet unless you are told to do so. The unless-clause comes after the main clause. No comma is needed before unless here. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Read and write correctly: do not open this booklet unless you are told to do so" Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.
